post.summary: Post-OIDC-login handler
post.description: Called by the frontend after every successful Authentik OIDC callback. Creates a User row on first login. Returns ToS acceptance status so the frontend can show the acceptance modal if needed.

get.summary: Current user's display state (T-245)
get.description: Tokens are HttpOnly cookies now — the frontend can't decode them for display state. Returns the same claims AuthMiddleware already enriched from the DB on every authenticated request.

get.summary: Start the OIDC login redirect (ARCH §6.4 step 1-2)
get.description: Generates state (CSRF), nonce, and a PKCE S256 challenge; stores them server-side in Redis keyed by a transient cookie; redirects the browser to Authentik's authorize endpoint. No response body — always a 302. `prompt_login`/`login_hint` are for post-invite and post-signup flows that need to force a fresh login pre-filled with the verified email, rather than silently reusing an unrelated existing SSO session.

get.summary: OIDC callback — server-side code+PKCE exchange (ARCH §6.4 steps 7-11)
get.description: Validates state, exchanges the code + PKCE verifier with Authentik server-side, validates the id_token nonce, provisions/looks up the user, sets the iqbalai_access/iqbalai_refresh cookies, and redirects to the caller's dashboard. Any failure redirects to a clean error page — never a hang, never a 500 for an untrusted callback.

302.description: Redirect to the dashboard, or to a login error page

post.summary: Refresh the access token from the iqbalai_refresh cookie (ARCH §6.9)
post.description: Reads the opaque iqbalai_refresh reference, resolves it to the real Authentik refresh token server-side, exchanges it for a new access token, and rotates the reference (single-use). No request body.

post.summary: Server-side logout (ARCH §6.8)
post.description: Revokes the refresh token at Authentik, clears both session cookies, and blacklists the access token's jti until it would have naturally expired. Works even with an already-expired or invalid access cookie — logout must always succeed. No request body, no response body.

validation alias lets `model_validate(record)` read it straight off the

API contract (and the generated typed client) is unchanged.
